<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|HOLY weeke. 76|THE GOSPEL|CHA. XXVI.}}</noinclude>{{sc|the nevv testament, vvhich shal be shed for many vnto remission of sinnes}}. {{verse|chapter=26|verse=29}}† And I say to you, I vvil not drinke from henceforth of this {{sup|‖}} fruite of the vine, vntil that day vvhen I shal drinke it vvith you nevv in the kingdom of my father. {{verse|chapter=26|verse=30}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text={{sc|Thvrsday}} night.}}And an hymne being said, they vvent forth vnto Mount-oliuet.

{{verse|chapter=26|verse=31}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The {{sc|Noctvrne}} of Mattins in the Churches Seruice, answereth to this night part of our Sauiours Passion. and so consequently the other Canonical houres to the rest.}}Then {{sc|Iesvs}} saith to them, Al you shal be scandalized in me, in this night. For it is vvritten, ''I vvil strike the Pastor, and the sheepe of the flocke shal be dispersed''.{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Zach. 13, 7.''}} {{verse|chapter=26|verse=32}}† But after I shal be risen againe, I vvil goe before you into Galilee. {{verse|chapter=26|verse=33}}† And Peter answering, said to him, Although al shal be scandalized in thee, I vvil neuer be scandalized. {{verse|chapter=26|verse=34}}† {{sc|Iesvs}} said to him, Amen I say to thee, that in this night before the cocke crovv, thou shalt denie me thrise. {{verse|chapter=26|verse=35}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Io. 13, 38.''}}* Peter saith to him, Yea though I should die vvith thee, I vvil not denie thee. Likevvise also said al the Disciples.

{{verse|chapter=26|verse=36}}† Then {{sc|Iesvs}} commeth vvith them into a village called Gethsémani: and he said to his Disciples, Sitte you here til I goe yonder, and pray. {{verse|chapter=26|verse=37}}† And taking to him Peter and the tvvo sonnes of Zebedee, he began to vvaxe sorovvful and to be sad. {{verse|chapter=26|verse=38}}† Then he saith to them: My soul is sorovvful euen vnto death: stay here, and vvatch vvith me. {{verse|chapter=26|verse=39}}† And being gone forvvard a litle, he fel vpon his face, praying, and saying, My Father, if it be possible, let this chalice passe from me. neuerthelesse {{sup|‖}} not as I vvil, but as thou. {{verse|chapter=26|verse=40}}† And he commeth to his Disciples, and findeth them sleeping, and he saith to Peter, Euen so? Could you not vvatch one houre vvith me? {{verse|chapter=26|verse=41}}† {{sup|‖}} Watch ye, and pray that ye enter not into tentation. The spirit in deede is prompt, but the flesh vveake. {{verse|chapter=26|verse=42}}† Againe the second time he vvent, and prayed, saying, My Father, if this chalice may not passe, but I must drinke it, thy vvil be done. {{verse|chapter=26|verse=43}}† And he commeth againe, and findeth them sleeping: for their eyes vvere become heauy. {{verse|chapter=26|verse=44}}† And leauing them, he went againe: and he prayed the third time, saying the self same vvord. {{verse|chapter=26|verse=45}}† Then he commeth to his Disciples, and saith to them, Sleepe ye now and take rest: behold the houre approcheth, and the Sonne of man shal be betrayed into the hands of sinners. {{verse|chapter=26|verse=46}}† Rise, let vs goe: behold he approcheth that shal betray me.

{{verse|chapter=26|verse=47}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Io. 18, 3.''}}* As he yet spake, behold Iudas one of the Tvvelue came, and vvith him a great multitude vvith swordes and clubbes, sent from the cheefe Priestes and the auncients of the people.<noinclude>{{rh|||And}}</noinclude>
